label: test-exists-and-reaches-changed-path
name: No test names a new primitive, or the tests call below the orchestration the diff changed, or a changed production formula is not mirrored in the tests that write the same field
description: What breaks: the changed code is never entered by a test. A new multi-producer ring (minfifo) with no test file (4614385493 'verifying multi-producer ordering, wrap-around, etc'); new tests call shard::xfer_gofs directly and never reach the changed cooperative drain orchestration (3960538961 'The added tests call shard::xfer_gofs directly'); the ktok formula changed in production while t_hwattention and t_hwattention_replay still write the old one (2771720147 'this should be updated in the ... tests as well'); a test swaps DmaQueue::acquire for dev->bypass_read_q with no sentence saying it is the same queue (2737853978 'is this indeed the same queue?'). Procedure: for every new reusable primitive under h/ and src/ require a file under t/ that names it; trace each new test's call to the production entry point and compare with the orchestration the diff changed; for every production formula the diff changes grep t/ for the same field name; for every test hunk that swaps a resource accessor require a sentence or comment. Distinct from check 3 (a test that exists but silently skips) and check 4 (two tests on one call).
disposition_reason: Checks 1-5 assume a test exists and reaches the code; reachability through the production caller and formula mirroring are a different, call-graph procedure. 4 rows over 4 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes: grep t/ for the new symbol, call graph from the test to the changed function, grep tests for the assigned field.

members.concern: The changed cooperative rodeo orchestration (help_drain_gof batching, fire_gof_rodeo_batch, dispatch_prepared_gof_xfers grouping and reservation handoff) is not exercised by any test: the new tests call shard::xfer_gofs directly and the existing 'gof rodeo populates and xfers to shard' test invokes population and transfer by hand; Wade asks for cases through the production drain path (mixed shards and layers, a reservation collision gap, branch fanout) asserting each target gets its KV exactly once, skipped positions stay untouched, and the forward-end drain finishes before scheduler-owned job storage is rebuilt.

detection.trigger: The diff changes an orchestration function (a drain, dispatch or grouping routine) and the tests added or cited by the PR call a lower-level function that the orchestration wraps, or set up state by hand instead of calling the production entry point.
detection.procedure: List the functions the diff changed in h/tron/models/model.hpp (help_drain_gof, wait_for_coop_gof, fire_gof_rodeo_batch, gof_rodeo_impl_batch) and grep t/ for each name; for each test hit read whether it calls the production entry point or re-implements its steps. List the branches inside the orchestration (single vs batch, reservation collision, fanout, mixed layers) and for each name the test that reaches it or write 'none'. Identify the lifetime contract the orchestration protects (drain finishes before job storage is rebuilt) and check whether any assertion observes it.
detection.question: Which test reaches the changed orchestration function through its production caller, and which assertion fails if a GOF is lost, delivered twice, or completed before the drain finishes?

members.quote: The added tests call `shard::xfer_gofs` directly. Even the existing test named "gof rodeo populates and xfers to shard" manually invokes population and transfer. Those cases do not exercise the new cooperative batching path
members.note: Same finding shape as 3960538177: 'Coverage gap:' headline, named scenarios, 'Please extend an existing CI suite', then the explicit disclaimer 'These are missing safety-contract checks; I have not observed a lost-GOF or premature-completion failure in the implementation' - he separates a coverage finding from a claimed bug. Note he read the existing test by name to show it also bypasses the path (test-name-promises-more-than-it-exercises). Head 7f80aa17da evidence: t_llama_unit.cpp:1020 TEST_CASE 'production GOF drain handles fanout layers and reservation gaps' with gof_indices{2,3,4} (nonzero), n_layers = 2, built on gof_test_model state - matches his asks (fanout, reservation gap, nonzero indices).

members.concern: The production formula for the ktok metadata field (token count within the 128-token page) changes from `((acmd_len - 1) % 128) + 1` to `(acmd_len % 128) + 1`; Wade asks that the tests that write the same field (t_hwattention, t_hwattention_replay) be updated to match, or offers to do it himself after merge.

detection.trigger: A hunk in src/ or h/ changes an arithmetic formula that assigns a hardware command field or a protocol value, and the same field name is assigned in one or more test files that are not in the diff.
detection.procedure: Take the assigned field name (here `fields.ktok`) and grep t/ for every assignment of it. For each hit compare the test's formula, after substituting the test's local variable definitions (e.g. num_tokens = token_idx + 1), with the new production formula. List tests whose formula is not equivalent, and tests the PR touches that still carry the old form.
detection.question: After this production formula change, does every test that assigns the same field compute the same value for the same token index, and is each such test either updated in this PR or shown to be already equivalent?

members.quote: this should be updated in the t_hwattention / t_hwattention_replay tests as well... else I can do it after you merge this I guess (I already have those changes staged)
members.note: Author answered that t_hwattention_replay already matches: 'in t_hwattention_replay, we set num_tokens to be token_idx+1, then subtract off one here. that is correct behior, if confusing.' Verified at c502e4d61a: t/t_hwattention_replay.cpp:391 `num_tokens = token_idx + 1` and :549 `ktok = ((num_tokens - 1) % 128) + 1`, so ktok = (token_idx % 128) + 1; t/t_hwattention.cpp:1292 keeps `((num_tokens - 1) % 128) + 1` and :825 a literal 128; neither test file changed between d306b805ce and c502e4d61a for this. Whether the worker's acmd_len equals a token index (so the two forms agree) is not verified here. Wade approved after the explanation without replying.

members.concern: Wade asks whether the new lock-free queue (minfifo, a multi-producer single-consumer ring) will get a unit test that checks multi-producer ordering and index wrap-around, because the first push had no test file.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a new reusable primitive (a new header plus source under h/ and src/, here a concurrency data structure with its own invariants) and the file list contains no new or changed file under t/ that names it.
detection.procedure: List files in the diff; for every new class or free function declared in a new header, grep t/ at HEAD for its name (`git grep -n <name> HEAD -- t/`). If nothing hits, read the header's design comment (here Note [minfifo design]) and list the invariants it states (ordering, wrap-around, full/empty behaviour, concurrent writers) as the test cases to ask for.
detection.question: Does any test under t/ exercise the new primitive's stated invariants (ordering across producers, wrap-around, full and empty states)?

members.quote: Are you going to build a unit-test for this? Seems it should warrant one... verifying multi-producer ordering, wrap-around, etc
members.note: At the reviewed commit 64ea13a671 the PR had no t/ file. The author's commit 'add unit test include other Preview feedback' added t/t_minfifo.cpp (254 lines) with cases 'sequence wraparound over many rounds', 'fill to capacity', '4 producers x 256 items - all received exactly once', 'per-producer FIFO order preserved under concurrency' (read at b8739108f7:t/t_minfifo.cpp). Wade named the exact invariants the Note [minfifo design] comment in h/pos/minfifo.hpp states.

members.concern: The test replaced `DmaQueue::acquire(dev, DMA_DIRECTION_RX, ...)` with `dev->bypass_read_q`; Wade asks whether the device's bypass_read_q is the same queue the old code acquired, that is, whether the test still exercises the same path.

detection.trigger: A test hunk replaces a resource acquisition (queue, buffer, device handle) with a different accessor without a comment and without a PR-body sentence describing it.
detection.procedure: Read DmaQueue::acquire and the definition of bypass_read_q (grep -rn 'bypass_read_q' h/ src/) to see whether acquire returns the same object or a fresh queue; check whether other tests or production code use bypass_read_q for the same direction; ask the author to state the intent in a comment or commit message.
detection.question: Is the replaced accessor the same object with the same semantics, or did the test's behavior change, and where is that stated?

members.quote: is this indeed the same queue?
